headline: A derivative is the slope of a curve at one instant, and the power rule finds it in one step.
tldr: A derivative measures how fast something changes at an exact moment. It is defined as a limit of slopes over smaller and smaller gaps. For powers of x, the power rule gives the answer directly: bring the exponent down and subtract one.
summary: The lecture starts from average rate of change, shrinks the interval to get the instantaneous rate, defines the derivative as a limit, then shortcuts the limit for powers of x with the power rule and works examples, including constants and sums.
takeaways: The **derivative** is the slope of the tangent line at a point.
It is defined as a **limit** of secant slopes.
The **power rule** turns xⁿ into n·xⁿ⁻¹.
Derivatives of **sums** split term by term.
exam_focus: Power rule and when it applies
The limit definition of the derivative

sections.title: Average vs instant rate of change
sections.summary: Average rate is slope over an interval; shrinking the interval gives the instant rate.
cues: What is an average rate of change?

points.text: The **average rate of change** is the slope of the secant line between two points.
Shrinking the interval turns the secant into the **tangent**.

terms.definition: A line through two points on a curve.
A line touching the curve at one point with the same slope.

sections.title: The limit definition
sections.summary: The derivative is the limit of secant slopes as the gap goes to zero.

points.text: **f′(x)** is the limit of [f(x+h) − f(x)] / h as h → 0.
sub: h is the width of the gap

points.text: For f(x) = x², the limit simplifies to **2x**.

terms.definition: The value an expression approaches as a variable approaches some value.

formulas.name: Limit definition
formulas.meaning: The slope at x is the limit of slopes over shrinking gaps.

mistakes: Forgetting to cancel h before taking the limit.

sections.title: The power rule
sections.summary: For xⁿ the derivative is n·xⁿ⁻¹; constants vanish and sums split.

points.text: **Power rule:** bring the exponent down, then subtract one.
Differentiate **sums** one term at a time.

formulas.name: Power rule
formulas.meaning: Works for any real exponent n.

mistakes: Subtracting one from the exponent before bringing it down.
